### Changed
- **`components.kserve-runtime-configs` follows the `0.3.x` line** (giantswarm/kserve#82). kserve-runtime-configs 0.3.0 adds `kserve.llmisvcConfigs.images.<preset>.<container>`, a per-config image override beside `imageRegistry`; its default render is byte-identical to 0.2.4's, and the meta chart's `kserve-runtime-configs:` block passes nothing new. The BOM example pins `0.3.0`.
### Fixed
- **`modelServing.prepull.nodeSelector` set by an installation renders alone** (giantswarm/agent-platform#562). Karpenter's `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-gpu-manufacturer: nvidia` was the values default in both charts, and Helm merges maps: a selector an installation set rendered next to the default key — a DaemonSet no node matched — and a `null` for the key was coalesced away when the meta chart forwarded its values, so the README's "or another selector here" was not reachable, and an installation whose GPU nodes are not launched by Karpenter stripped the key with a post-renderer. Both values files now carry `nodeSelector: {}` and the template holds the default (`agent-platform.modelServing.prepull.nodeSelector`): empty renders Karpenter's label, a set map renders alone, the pool's label (`gpuPool.nodeSelector`) is merged under either; a non-string label value fails the render naming the key. `tests/verify-mirrored-values.py` counts an empty mapping as a leaf, so a copy that kept the map is drift; `make verify-model-serving-policies` asserts the selector cases, the guard, and a selector set on the meta chart reaching the DaemonSet alone. README "Pre-pulling the runtime image"; UPGRADE.md.
- **The pre-pull DaemonSet is a hook object: an image that cannot be pulled yet no longer fails the connectivity upgrade** (giantswarm/agent-platform#563). As a release resource the DaemonSet was in the release's wait, and a release's wait counts a DaemonSet ready by its pods: helm-controller from 1.6 waits with the kstatus poller, which needs every pod of a DaemonSet Ready (Helm 3's legacy waiter, still on helm-controller 1.4, takes `maxUnavailable: 100%` as ready once the pods are scheduled — the fleet runs both). A pod whose image cannot be pulled is never Ready, so one listed image not yet pullable — a runtime image or a `prepull.modelPresets` image still being built, a registry outage — held the pods in `ImagePullBackOff`, timed the wait out and marked the whole connectivity release failed and retried, every other object applied. The DaemonSet now carries `helm.sh/hook: post-install,post-upgrade,post-rollback` (weight 0, `before-hook-creation`): created after the release's objects are applied and waited for, waited for by nobody — a hook's `WatchUntilReady` watches Jobs and Pods only, in Helm 3, Helm 4 and helm-controller alike — so a missing image leaves the pods retrying on the kubelet's backoff and the release Ready; the next event replaces the DaemonSet and the pods come back on images already present. A hook object is not Helm's to delete on uninstall, so a `pre-delete` hook Job (`<release>-model-serving-prepull-cleanup`, the hook include `agent-platform.hooks.job`; the identity `<release>-hooks` is created for that event too, with `delete` on exactly that DaemonSet) removes it. The deny-all policy stays a release resource. `make verify-model-serving-policies` asserts the hook shape, the cleanup Job, the identity's rule and that `prepull.enabled: false` renders neither; `verify-serving-slice` holds the identity to the pre-delete event alone with the cache off; `verify-gpu-pool` leaves the DaemonSet out of the golden comparison while `origin/main` renders it as a release resource. README "Pre-pulling the runtime image"; UPGRADE.md.
